source.snippet: Curious to know how are you interviewing engineers? Do you have a no-LLM policy? Are take-home tests worth it? How do you make sure engineer is a 'good' engineer?

problem_statement: Engineering hiring managers and CTOs lack reliable, bias-resistant methods to evaluate software engineer candidates now that LLMs make traditional coding tests trivially completable, creating uncertainty about signal validity in technical interviews.
target_segment: Engineering managers, CTOs, and technical recruiters at software companies hiring developers in 2026
notes: Buyer signal: companies spend significant budget on recruiting and hiring tools (HackerRank, Codility, etc. are known paid products). The agentic-era framing is fresh (2026-07-20) and the question has active engagement. Opportunity: interview platform or assessment methodology explicitly designed for the LLM era — e.g., live pair-programming evaluation, design/architecture walkthroughs, or AI-usage-allowed assessments that test judgment rather than syntax recall.
